name: Checkout.com
summary: Checkout.com processes online payments for large merchants, handling more than $1 billion in e-commerce volume a day.
overview: Checkout.com provides online payment processing, acquiring and fraud tools for large global merchants.
bull_case: Large volumes, renewed growth and profitability make the reset valuation look conservative if growth continues.
bear_case: Adyen and Stripe are bigger and well funded, and payment processing margins keep falling.
latest_round: September 2025: $12B valuation set with an employee share buyback

intelligence.description: Checkout.com provides online payment processing, acquiring and fraud tools for large global merchants.
company: Checkout.com was founded by Guillaume Pousaz and processes online payments for large merchants around the world. It says it handles more than $1 billion of e-commerce payment volume a day and expected to process over $300 billion in 2025.

At its peak in January 2022 the company was valued at $40 billion. In September 2025 it announced an employee share buyback at a $12 billion valuation, alongside net revenue growth above 30% in its core business and a return to full-year profitability.
intelligence.why_it_matters: Checkout.com is one of the clearest examples of a 2021-era valuation being reset, and a benchmark for how private payments companies are priced against Adyen and Stripe.

changed.text: The company lowers its internal valuation as fintech multiples fall.
An employee buyback sets a $12B valuation as the company returns to profitability.

takeaways: The valuation is down 70% from its 2022 peak.
The business is growing and profitable again.
Payment processing is a scale business with thin margins.
It competes directly with Adyen and Stripe for large merchants.
